# Chapter 19 - sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) To the provider: The application layer, OS/runtime, physical and network
- the shop software and its patching are now theirs. Staying with FastGoods:
Data and access - the customer database, encryption decisions within the
platform's settings, who can log in and with what MFA. Unchanged: R1 - account
takeover is an access question, and the top row of the model never moves; R3's
data ownership likewise stays, with only the mechanics shifting. (2) Tier:
Critical - it reads customer order data (personal data, R3 adjacent).
Evidence: ISO 27001 certificate or SOC 2 Type II, a security policy and
sub-processor list, data-residency statement, and its own supplier register for
the model provider behind it. Non-negotiable clauses: The Article 28 DPA
(personal data is processed) and breach notification within 24 hours; audit
rights close behind. (3) The GDPR's 72-hour clock runs from FastGoods *becoming
aware* - Monday 09:00 - but the exposure ran all weekend, the delay itself
must be explained, and FastGoods' customers were unprotected for 63 hours it
cannot account for; a regulator will ask why the contract allowed it. Clause:
"The supplier shall notify FastGoods of any personal-data breach without undue
delay and at latest within 24 hours of detection, with known facts and a named
contact, updating as facts develop." (4) Concentration hiding as fourth-party
risk: Three of four rows share platform X, so one platform incident hits shop,
mail and analytics at once - CrowdStrike's 19 July 2024 is the illustration
(Chapter 15). Measure: Move the availability fallback off-platform - e.g. the
static "we are down, orders resume shortly" page and the customer-notification
channel hosted elsewhere - so the concentration loses its single point of
communication failure. (5) Test: Switch checkout to the fallback provider (or
the pre-agreed manual flow) and process one real transaction end to end.
Evidence: A dated test record with the transaction reference - Chapter 16's
system-generated kind. If never run: The exit exists only as Chapter 12 defines
the untested plan - a document, not a capability - and a payment-provider
outage converts directly into R2 at full length, with the fallback discovered
broken exactly when the checkout is dark.
